title: analytics policy evaluator and row-filtering enforcement for usage views
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Console analytics endpoints (usage views, per-route dashboards, token-level breakdowns) need a unified, low-latency policy enforcement layer that applies RBAC and attribute-based row filtering before sensitive aggregates or raw usage rows are returned. Current ad-hoc checks are scattered in query builders and service handlers, leading to gaps for delegated access, inconsistent audit logs, and duplicated filtering logic across endpoints.

Goal: Build a central 'Analytics Policy Evaluator' service/middleware that: 1) evaluates access policies (org, team, role, delegated principals, entitlements) and produces query-safe filters that can be pushed down to the analytics storage layer when possible; 2) emits audit events for every enforcement decision; 3) caches policy decisions for performance while maintaining correctness for permission changes; 4) provides a fallback post-query filter for complex policies that can't be expressed in the OLAP pushdown; 5) integrates with the entitlement-syncer (ENG-15005) and the Console rollout controls (canary/A/B rollout keys).

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Enforcement location: We compared three options: gateway-level enforcement (fast but limited context), service-layer middleware (good context, mid-latency), and DB row-level policies (secure but hard to express complex rules). We selected a hybrid approach: produce pushdown predicates for ClickHouse/OLAP when expressible, otherwise use service-layer post-filtering. This balances security, expressivity, and latency.
- Policy representation: Use an intermediate, serializable 'policy AST' that can be converted into SQL WHERE fragments or an in-memory predicate evaluator. Keeping the AST avoids duplication and enables deterministic caching.
- Caching: Cache (user, org, dataset, query-shape) -> compiled predicate with a short TTL (60s) and invalidation hooks fed by entitlement-syncer events. Trade-off: improves QPS but requires careful invalidation to avoid stale access.
- Audit: Every request evaluated will emit a compact audit event (user, principal, policy-id, reason, pushdown-applied true/false) to the audit topic. This is required for compliance and later queryability.
- Performance target: added latency for enforcement must be <= 20ms p95 on median usage view queries when pushdown is applied, and <= 50ms p95 when post-filtering is used. Memory overhead must be bounded per worker.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Prototype policy AST + small evaluator + unit tests (ENG-49921-pt1).
2) Integrate pushdown generator for ClickHouse and validate predicate equivalence with existing filters (ENG-49921-pt2).
3) Add caching layer + invalidation hook from entitlement-syncer events (ENG-15005).
4) Add audit emission, telemetry, and synthetic benchmarks.
5) Gradual rollout: behind feature flag, start with non-blocking audit-only mode for 48 hours, then soft-enforce (block only if match from whitelist), then full enforcement with canary per org.

Acceptance criteria: 
- All analytics endpoints (usage-rows, per-token cost breakdown, per-route time series) route through the evaluator when feature flag on.
- Pushdown predicates are correct for the policy test-suite (automated Golden queries).
- Integration tests emulate entitlement changes and confirm invalidation within 60s.
- Audit events appear in the audit topic and include enforcement decisions.
- Performance target met on staging: enforcement overhead <= 20ms p95 for pushdown flow.

Rollout plan and mitigations: 
- Start in audit-only mode to collect enforcement outcomes without blocking.
- Canary with 1% of orgs, monitor error rate and median latency.
- If unexpected blocking occurs, rollback to audit-only via feature flag and use decision logs to triage.

Open questions: 
- Should policies be authored in a high-level DSL (future) or configured by a UI in Console? (deliver DSL later; ship baked-in mappings now)
- How to handle delegated token scopes that expire mid-query? We will snapshot entitlements at request start time.

Links and artifacts: 
- Design doc (confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/analytics-policy-evaluator
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8213
- Bench dashboards (staging): https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/analytics-policy/enforcer-staging

Notes: This ticket focuses on backend enforcement and query pushdown. UI changes to surface blocked rows or permission errors are tracked in a follow-up PM ticket.

comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Kaur: Initial spike finished. Prototype AST and basic evaluator in repo under experiments/policy-eval. Pushdown generator translates simple role filters to ClickHouse WHERE clauses. Need to validate against current query builder for usage-rows.

2025-02-15 - Benji Morales: Benchmarked prototype locally. Pushdown path adds ~8ms median on top of baseline; post-filter path currently ~42ms median. Plan to optimize in worker by memoizing compiled predicates.

2025-02-18 - Priya Nair (Security): Reviewed threat model. Requested explicit audit fields: policy-id, evaluated-by, and request-hash. Also requested an option to force DB-side enforcement for high-risk datasets. Marked security_review_required=true.
2025-02-20 - Benji Morales: Implemented audit emission to topic analytics-audit-v2. Added feature flag analytics.policy_enforcer.v1 with modes [audit-only, soft-enforce, enforce].

2025-02-24 - Staff Engineer Review (Luca Chen): Suggested moving TTL to 30s for highly dynamic entitlement workloads and adding compatibility tests against the entitlement-syncer events. Also suggested batching invalidation events to avoid thundering herd.
2025-02-26 - Benji Morales: Opened PR #8213 for proto integration and PR #8255 for caching. Added e2e test harness to the CI pipeline to run a small matrix of delegated tokens and dataset shapes.
2025-02-28 - Aisha Kaur: Kicked off staging run in audit-only mode for 24h to collect data. Next steps: evaluate staging logs, tune TTL, and prepare canary plan for 1% orgs next week.
